title: Indiana → Carolinas Stamp Sprint
subtitle: Fly into Indianapolis, out of Charlotte. Four days, Thursday to Sunday, one stamp per unit.
chips: IN · KY · TN · AL · NC · SC

days.title: Fly to Indianapolis
days.html:
✈︎

SFO → IND after work

United flies SFO–IND nonstop. Check Google Flights for the latest evening departure.

One-way rental: pick up at IND, drop at CLT. Expect a drop fee; compare on Costco Travel.

Sleep near the airport. Tomorrow starts at 6:55 AM ET, so grab breakfast to go.

Time zones on this trip: Day 1 flips ET → CT → ET → CT. Russell Cave (AL) is Central; Chattanooga onward is Eastern. Every time in this book is local.

days.title: Lincoln Country
days.tzline: 3 time-zone flips today (ET → CT → ET → CT)
days.cut: Lincoln Boyhood closes for lunch 12–1 and shuts at 3 CT. Be there before noon.

days.title: Caves & Atoms
days.tzline: Central → Eastern after Russell Cave (lose 1 hr)
days.cut: Oak Ridge closes at 4 PM and Obed at 5. Keep Chattanooga quick.

days.title: Through the Gap
days.cut: Mill Springs, Cumberland Gap and Andrew Johnson all close at 4 PM.

days.title: Over the Smokies
days.cut: Book the CLT flight for ~5 PM or later. Kings Mountain has almost no phone signal, so load directions to CLT before you arrive.

stops.name: George Rogers Clark NHP
stops.acc: The memorial itself is up 33 steps and opens on request. Skip it; the stamp is in the visitor center.
stops.about: Honors the 1779 winter march in which Clark’s small frontier force captured British-held Fort Sackville on this spot, securing the Old Northwest for the new United States. The granite rotunda by the Wabash River went up in the 1930s.

stops.tz: Cross into Central time: gain 1 hr
stops.name: Lincoln Boyhood NMem
stops.addr: 3027 E South St, Lincoln City, IN 47552
stops.warn: Tightest hours of the trip. Arrive before noon.
stops.about: Abraham Lincoln lived on this farm from age 7 to 21. His mother, Nancy Hanks Lincoln, died here in 1818 and is buried on the grounds.

stops.name: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace NHP
stops.acc: The Memorial Building sits atop 56 steps. Skip it; the stamp is in the visitor center.
stops.about: A symbolic log cabin sits inside a marble-and-granite memorial on the farm where Lincoln was born in 1809. The 56 steps up to it stand for the 56 years of his life.

stops.name: Mammoth Cave NP
stops.addr: Mammoth Cave Visitor Center, 1 Mammoth Cave Pkwy, Mammoth Cave, KY 42259
stops.hrs: Daily · hours vary by season (summer ~8–6:30 CT)
stops.ok: One closer on the 64 national parks list.
stops.about: The longest known cave system in the world, with more than 400 miles mapped so far. The visitor center has exhibits on the cave and the people who explored it.

stops.name: Stones River NB
stops.warn: In winter this arrival is just 15 minutes before close. Don’t linger at Mammoth Cave.
stops.about: Site of a bloody battle fought from Dec 31, 1862 to Jan 2, 1863. The Union win lifted Northern morale right as the Emancipation Proclamation took effect.

stops.name: Murfreesboro, TN
stops.note: Best Western, TBD. Tomorrow starts at 6:55 AM CT for Russell Cave.

stops.name: Russell Cave NM
stops.acc: The visitor center entrance has a steep incline and a narrow doorway.
stops.about: A huge limestone rock shelter that people used as a seasonal home for more than 10,000 years. It’s one of the most complete records of prehistoric life in the Southeast.

stops.name: Chickamauga & Chattanooga NMP
stops.addr: 110 Point Park Rd, Lookout Mountain, TN 37350
stops.acc: Small lot behind the building. Point Park’s entry fee is covered by your pass.
stops.about: The first national military park, created in 1890. Point Park looks down on Chattanooga and Moccasin Bend, where the 1863 “Battle Above the Clouds” was fought.

stops.name: Manhattan Project NHP
stops.addr: 461 W Outer Dr, Oak Ridge, TN 37830
stops.where: Visitor Center, inside the Children’s Museum of Oak Ridge
stops.warn: Hard cutoff at 4 PM. Grab the traditional stamp and the Oak Ridge third of the three-part stamp.
stops.about: Oak Ridge was the “Secret City,” built from scratch in 1942–43 to enrich uranium for the first atomic bombs. The park is split between Oak Ridge, Hanford and Los Alamos, hence the three-part stamp.

stops.name: Obed Wild & Scenic River
stops.where: Visitor Center bookstore, on the left as you walk in
stops.about: Protects the Obed and its tributaries cutting deep sandstone gorges into the Cumberland Plateau. It’s best known among whitewater paddlers and rock climbers.

stops.name: Big South Fork NRRA
stops.addr: Bandy Creek Visitor Center, Oneida, TN 37841
stops.where: Bandy Creek Visitor Center, passport counter on the window sill
stops.ok: One stamp covers the unit. Stearns (KY) is skipped; it’s only open Thu–Sun in summer.
stops.about: The Big South Fork of the Cumberland River carves a gorge lined with sandstone arches and bluffs along the Tennessee–Kentucky line.

stops.name: Somerset, KY
stops.note: Best Western, TBD. Tomorrow starts at 7:50 AM, heading north to Camp Nelson first.

stops.name: Camp Nelson NM
stops.ok: If it’s closed, a dated stamp is kept in a box on the front porch.
stops.about: A Union supply depot that became Kentucky’s largest recruiting and training center for U.S. Colored Troops, and a refuge for their families. It became a national monument in 2018.

stops.name: Mill Springs Battlefield NM
stops.about: A January 1862 Union victory, one of the first significant ones of the war. It joined the park system in 2019, making it one of the newest units.

stops.name: Cumberland Gap NHP
stops.ok: Good lunch stop in Middlesboro. The drive up to Pinnacle Overlook won’t fit today; Andrew Johnson closes at 4.
stops.about: The natural pass through the Appalachians that Daniel Boone’s Wilderness Road followed. Hundreds of thousands of settlers crossed it heading west.

stops.name: Andrew Johnson NHS
stops.warn: Closes at 4 PM. Use 101 N College St, not the HQ address GPS sometimes shows. The center may lock briefly during Homestead tours on short-staffed days.
stops.about: Preserves the tailor shop and homes of the 17th president, who took office after Lincoln’s assassination. He is buried in the national cemetery here.

stops.name: Gatlinburg, TN
stops.note: Best Western, TBD. Sugarlands is 13 min before town. If it’s still open as you pass, grab the stamp tonight and sleep in.

stops.name: Great Smoky Mountains NP
stops.acc: A parking tag is required for stops over 15 minutes. A quick stamp stop should be under that, but check the current rule.
stops.about: The most visited national park in the country, straddling the Tennessee–North Carolina line. Another one for the 64 parks list.

stops.name: Blue Ridge Parkway
stops.about: A 469-mile scenic road linking the Smokies to Shenandoah. The visitor center near Asheville has a film and a large interactive map of the whole parkway.

stops.name: Carl Sandburg Home NHS
stops.addr: 1800 Little River Rd, Flat Rock, NC 28731
stops.where: Visitor Center / Park Store, ground floor of the Sandburg Home
stops.acc: The house sits up a hill from the main lot. Call ahead about accessible parking near the house, and allow extra time.
stops.about: Connemara, the farm where poet Carl Sandburg spent his last 22 years. Descendants of his wife Lilian’s prize-winning dairy goats still live on the farm.

stops.name: Cowpens NB
stops.about: In January 1781, Daniel Morgan’s mixed force routed Banastre Tarleton’s troops here in under an hour. It was a turning point of the war in the South.

stops.name: Kings Mountain NMP
stops.warn: Phone reception is very limited here. Load directions to CLT before you arrive.
stops.about: In October 1780, frontier militia known as the Overmountain Men defeated a Loyalist force on this ridge. Thomas Jefferson later called it the turn of the tide of the Revolution.

stops.name: CLT → home
stops.note: Return the one-way rental, then fly home. A flight around 5 PM or later leaves buffer.
stops.title: Charlotte → home
